methodology: The decomposition process involved analyzing both the original research topic and the generated technical specification to extract independent and self-contained atomic units. Each unit was evaluated for technical specificity and unambiguity, ensuring that they could be implemented as single requirements. The truth table of the JK flip-flop was broken down into distinct behaviors based on the input combinations of J and K, while the generated specification was analyzed for its description of combinational logic and timing behavior. This resulted in two sets of atomic information units, one from the original topic and one from the generated specification.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The JK flip-flop has a truth table defining its behavior based on inputs J and K.
When J=0 and K=0, Q remains Qold.
When J=0 and K=1, Q is set to 0.
When J=1 and K=0, Q is set to 1.
When J=1 and K=1, Q toggles to ~Qold.
The module 'top_module' implements the JK flip-flop behavior.
The output Q is updated on the rising edge of the clock signal.
spec_atomic_units: The top module header definition includes the interface definition and behavior.
The outputs of the combinational logic circuit are derived from inputs J and K based on the truth table.
When J=0 and K=0, Q remains unchanged (Q=Qold).
When J=0 and K=1, Q is reset to 0 (Q=0).
When J=1 and K=0, Q is set to 1 (Q=1).
When J=1 and K=1, Q toggles its state (Q=~Qold).
State Retention Logic retains the previous state of Q when both J and K are 0.
Reset Logic sets Q to 0 when J is 0 and K is 1.
Set Logic sets Q to 1 when J is 1 and K is 0.
Toggle Logic toggles Q when both J and K are 1.
Signal flow optimization minimizes the number of gates used.
The module implements timing logic with a register Q updated on the positive edge of clk.
